address noun

where someone lives or gets post

also postal address, home address, email address, e-mail address, address a letter, addressed to, zip code, postcode, post code

modern

Traupman 268: īnscrīptiō cursuālis
Traupman 261, 309: īnscrīptiō ēlectronica, e-mail address
M-O s.v. address: inscriptio cursualis

īnscrīptiō, īnscrīptiōnis f.

noun, third declension · Declension on Wiktionary

an address (on a letter, for email)

Classically an inscription or the title of a book (Cic. Att. 16.11.4). The address is what is written on a letter, and the verb is classical: epistulam īnscrīptam patrī suō, a letter addressed to his father (Cic. Att. 6.3.8).

Other words

  • Ubi habitās? — Where do you live? (What is your address?)

    also used · classical · Ter. Eun. 320e: Ubi habitat?

  • īnscrībō, īnscrībere, īnscrīpsī, īnscrīptum — address (a letter, a parcel)

    verb, third conjugation · also used · classical · Cic. Att. 8.5.2: fasciculum, quī est M’. Curiō īnscrīptus; Cic. Att. 6.3.8: epistulam īnscrīptam patrī suō; Traupman 268 · Conjugation on Wiktionary

    The person written to in the dative.

Examples

  • Unde est? — Tantundem. — Ubi habitat? — Nē id quidem.

    Where’s she from? — No idea either. — Where does she live? — I don’t even know that.Ter. Eun. 320c–321

  • tū fasciculum, quī est M’. Curiō īnscrīptus, velim cūrēs ad eum perferendum

    please see that the packet addressed to Manius Curius gets to himCic. Att. 8.5.2

  • numerus cursuālis (dīrēctōrius)

    a zip code, postcodeTraupman 410

See also post a letter, envelope, postcard, address.
